artworks.title: Odysseus and his men blinding Polyphemus (Eleusis Amphora, detail)
artworks.description: The oldest surviving Cyclops scene — Nobody's cunning stake earns Poseidon's endless enmity after the lotus and the cave.

artworks.title: Ulysses Deriding Polyphemus
artworks.description: Dawn bursts over the escaping fleet while the blinded giant, half cloud and half mountain, writhes above the bay — Turner's answer to Odyssey 9, all light where the cave was all dark.

artworks.title: The Blinding of Polyphemus
artworks.description: Allori's Mannerist stake — Odysseus and his men drive the heated timber into the sleeping Cyclops' eye.

artworks.title: Odysseus and Polyphemus
artworks.description: Böcklin's Symbolist confrontation — the hero facing the one-eyed shepherd before the wine and the name Nobody.

artworks.title: Landscape with Polyphemus
artworks.description: Poussin's Hermitage landscape — the Cyclops tiny on the mountain above Arcadian calm, Odyssey IX's giant as a speck of threat.

films.title: Ulysses
films.description: Kirk Douglas' Odysseus faces the Cyclops on screen — the stake, the name Nobody, and the wine that blinds the giant.

films.title: The Odyssey
films.description: The miniseries gives Book IX its runtime — lotus forgetfulness, then Polyphemus' cave before Poseidon's wrath begins.

popCulture.title: Odyssey
popCulture.description: Book IX — Lotus-eaters and the Cyclops — remains the poem's first great adventure told in Alcinous' hall.

popCulture.title: Polyphemus
popCulture.description: Poseidon's son, the one-eyed shepherd — wine, Nobody, and a heated stake still define the Cyclops for every retelling.
